memory_update.text: Add TIC Solutions as an underfollowed small-cap TIC and asset-integrity candidate for energy supplier qualification, inspection, compliance, and continuity assurance; verify energy and utilities revenue materiality.
Add MISTRAS Group as an underfollowed small-cap pure-play asset-integrity and inspection candidate with explicit power, nuclear, T&D, renewables, and oil and gas exposure.
Use Moody's and S&P Global as reference supplier-risk data platforms, not alpha-primary small-cap candidates, because both are mega-cap and energy exposure is likely diluted.

The strongest public-market mapping for this node may split into two subnodes: digital supplier-risk data platforms and physical TIC/asset-integrity providers. The latter appears more investable in the underfollowed US small/mid-cap lane.

Need to verify whether utility procurement, nuclear supplier qualification, transformer/grid equipment testing, and energy-project compliance create measurable revenue tailwinds for TIC, MG, MCO, or SPGI.
MCO is a reference anchor for the supplier-risk data layer, not an underfollowed energy pure-play; track only to map product category and competitive vocabulary.

ULS is a plausible TIC and grid-equipment qualification candidate, but market cap is above the ideal underfollowed range; keep only if later evidence shows unusually pure exposure to energy-grid certification and compliance bottlenecks.
MG is the cleanest small-cap candidate for energy asset integrity, NDT, inspection, and condition-monitoring exposure; verify energy revenue materiality and recurring versus turnaround-driven demand.
MEG is a speculative-shadow candidate for energy environmental compliance, methane, emissions testing, and permitting; it needs explicit energy customer/revenue evidence before promotion.

Private companies such as ISN, Avetta, DNV, ABS, and specialist nuclear/utility qualification platforms may dominate parts of supplier-risk and certification workflows, but this pass only retained US-listed public equities.

The investable node splits into three sublayers: supplier-risk data and procurement analytics; testing/inspection/certification and grid-code compliance; and operating-asset integrity/environmental compliance.

TIC Solutions is the best underfollowed US-listed candidate for this node because it combines Acuren inspection/NDT/asset-integrity services with NV5 engineering, geospatial, infrastructure, utility-services, and compliance capabilities; verify energy/utilities revenue materiality before Layer 2.

UL Solutions is not small-cap but is an unusually direct certification-gate candidate for grid-code compliance, renewables, storage, EV charging, utility product certification, and AI-enabled energy-management system certification.

Team Inc. should remain a speculative micro-cap exception only; relevance to inspection and energy asset-integrity is strong, but financial/liquidity risk and cyclicality must be checked before any prioritization.

Supplier-risk visibility for energy appears to split into two investable sublanes: diversified data/risk platforms such as Moody's and S&P Global, and more direct physical qualification/inspection gates such as TIC Solutions, UL Solutions, and Team Inc.

Many pure supplier-risk platforms relevant to energy and utilities, including Exiger, Interos, PCI Energy Solutions, Element, DNV/KEMA, and Integros-like inspection specialists, appear private or non-US-listed; public-market exposure may be indirect or diversified.

TIC Solutions may be the cleanest underfollowed public-market mapping for energy-adjacent TICC, asset integrity, geospatial utility data, and engineering compliance after the Acuren/NV5 merger; verify post-merger energy/utilities revenue mix.

Mistras Group is a small-cap asset-integrity/NDT candidate with direct power generation/transmission and oil/gas exposure; needs vertical revenue validation and evidence of growth from grid/power work.

UL Solutions is a reference leader for the certification bottleneck around electrical equipment, grid code compliance, renewables, batteries, and energy automation, but its market cap and attention level make it less suitable for the underfollowed lane.

True supplier-risk software/data vendors for energy procurement appear sparse among US-listed pure plays; many likely candidates are private, recently taken private, or embedded inside broad information-services companies. Later layers should search for procurement-platform and third-party-risk vendors with explicit utility/energy customer proof.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the universe for the energy supplier-risk visibility node into two lanes. Reference lane: large data platforms with explicit supplier-risk products that can serve utilities, energy operators, and industrial procurement teams, but whose energy exposure is likely diluted by broader enterprise data revenue. Underfollowed lane: smaller US-listed TIC and asset-integrity companies whose services are closer to physical qualification, inspection, and continuity assurance for energy assets, power generation, transmission, oil and gas, utilities, and infrastructure. This remains a speculative second-order node until energy-specific revenue mix, customer wins, and procurement/qualification use cases are verified. Expanded the node into a two-lane universe focused on energy supplier-risk visibility, testing, inspection, certification, compliance, and asset-integrity data. The reference lane is Moody's, because it directly frames energy supplier risk as a structural issue and sells supplier-risk data/analytics. The underfollowed lane contains US-listed TIC, asset-integrity, and environmental-compliance names whose energy exposure is plausible but must be verified for materiality before surviving later Serenity layers. Expanded the universe for the speculative second-order node where energy capital spending, grid interconnection complexity, nuclear/renewables qualification, and supplier continuity risk create demand for assurance, inspection, testing, certification, geospatial/asset-integrity, and supplier-risk data platforms.
